issues.title: Classify Lazurio Documentation in the Organization inventory
issues.question: Where should the public Lazurio Documentation repository live in the Human and Machine Organization inventory?
issues.impact: The repository needed one truthful local classification without changing its public GitHub owner or granting it Workspace runtime authority.
options: Register it as a runnable Workspace module with Team membership and a port lease.
Register it as a read-only productionspace repository while preserving Lazurio/documentation as the provider authority.

resolution.decision: Lazurio/documentation remains a public repository in the Lazurio GitHub Organization and is represented locally as productionspace/documentation in Human and Machine.
resolution.rationale: Documentation is a public production surface with its own Cloudflare publication gate. It is not a Team-owned Workspace application and therefore has no Launchpad Start action, runtime lease or port.
resolution.selected_option: Register it as a read-only productionspace repository while preserving Lazurio/documentation as the provider authority.
resolution.evidence: The reviewed Organization inventory was published; Organization Doctor, Lazurio synchronization and Launchpad readback confirmed the read-only productionspace representation.

issues.title: Confirm availability of advanced GitHub secret-scanning modes
issues.question: Can non-provider pattern scanning and validity checks be enabled for this public repository under the current GitHub Organization plan and policy?
issues.impact: GitHub secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot security updates remain enabled. The two additional modes are not available under the current Lazurio Organization plan.
options: Enable the advanced modes if the Organization plan exposes them and verify provider readback.
Keep standard secret scanning and push protection as the enforced baseline and document the advanced modes as unavailable.

resolution.decision: Keep the verified standard secret-scanning baseline and treat non-provider patterns plus partner validity checks as unavailable until the Organization plan changes.
resolution.rationale: Live GitHub readback identifies the Lazurio Organization as GitHub Free and both repository modes as disabled. GitHub's current product documentation makes these modes available to Organization repositories on GitHub Team with Secret Protection. The global recommended configuration is unenforced and is not evidence that the controls run on this repository.
resolution.selected_option: Keep standard secret scanning and push protection as the enforced baseline and document the advanced modes as unavailable.
resolution.evidence: GitHub REST readback on 2026-08-27 plus the current GitHub documentation for generic patterns and partner validity checks.

issues.title: Align local Wrangler runtime with the declared compatibility date
issues.question: Which reviewed Wrangler version should replace 4.92.0 so local Pages emulation supports compatibility date 2026-08-26?
issues.impact: Local Pages emulation now covers the declared compatibility date instead of relying only on Astro build and deployed-provider smoke.
options: Upgrade the pinned Wrangler version in a separate dependency PR and rerun build plus Pages emulation.
Keep 4.92.0 temporarily and treat CI plus a deployed preview smoke as the provider-runtime proof.

resolution.rationale: The reviewed version supports Node 22+, accepts compatibility date 2026-08-26 and keeps the existing Pages build and deployment contract unchanged.
resolution.selected_option: Upgrade the pinned Wrangler version in a separate dependency PR and rerun build plus Pages emulation.
resolution.evidence: The full build passed and Wrangler 4.127.0 served the generated Pages worker locally with 302 root redirect, 200 English page and exact content-index source commit.

issues.title: Triage dependency vulnerabilities reported on the default branch
issues.question: Which dependencies account for the 18 open GitHub vulnerability alerts, and which upgrades can be applied without breaking the pinned documentation stack?
issues.impact: GitHub reported 3 high, 9 moderate and 6 low dependency vulnerabilities during the Czech documentation push. The current gh identity received HTTP 404 when requesting alert details, so affected packages, reachability and fixed versions remained unverified.
options: Inspect the alerts with an identity that can read repository security events, then prepare a separate dependency-update PR with build and browser verification.
If GitHub's count is stale or refers only to unreachable development tooling, record the evidence and close or downgrade this issue without weakening the current security baseline.

resolution.decision: The 18 alerts are 17 Astro runtime advisories and one @astrojs/cloudflare adapter advisory; prepare one reviewed static-site upgrade instead of merging the individually incompatible Dependabot PRs.
resolution.rationale: Live GitHub API readback made the affected packages and patched versions visible. The existing Documentation is static and contains no Cloudflare runtime API usage, so removing the adapter is simpler and preserves its Pages deployment contract while allowing the patched Astro 7 family.
resolution.selected_option: Inspect the alerts with an identity that can read repository security events, then prepare a separate dependency-update PR with build and browser verification.
resolution.evidence: GitHub Dependabot alert readback on 2026-08-31; local Bun 1.3.14 frozen-install, content, build and Pages browser checks on the replacement branch.

issues.title: Decide how the pages present Lazurio's license so that the lazurio-license source can be renewed
issues.question: Which license do index, faq and it-administrators present as Lazurio's current license, while public-evidence and reference keep the FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 terms as the pinned Lazurio Root revision?
issues.impact: The re-verification of 2026-11-17 renewed 13 of the 14 sources due by 2026-11-29. lazurio-license was not renewed: the pinned LICENSE.md is unchanged on HumanAndMachines/Lazurio main, but the released Lazurio Platform uses Elastic License 2.0 with no automatic two-year Apache transition (LazurioPlatform LICENSE and docs/licensing.md). index and faq still say that Lazurio is currently source-available under FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0, and the IT table promises the Apache transition; public-evidence and reference label the FSL terms as the pinned revision. Choosing the current license statement for a public, trust-critical page is a product and legal decision, and an open proposal for it exists in pull request #48 (issue #42). The source expires on 2026-11-27, so the content check fails every pull request from 2026-11-28 until the pages change.
options: Settle the license statement in #48 or a dedicated pull request: present the Platform's Elastic-2.0 as current, keep the FSL terms labelled as the pinned Lazurio Root revision, re-pin lazurio-license to the Platform license and renew it. Recommended: it is the only way the pages stay true.
Keep the source expired and accept that no documentation pull request passes the check from 2026-11-28 until the pages are updated.

resolution.decision: Present Elastic-2.0 as the license of the released Lazurio Platform and keep FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 as the license of the earlier Lazurio root repository on index, faq, it-administrators and public-evidence, in both locales.
resolution.rationale: Both statements are true today: the root's LICENSE.md is unchanged, and LazurioPlatform's LICENSE and docs/licensing.md establish Elastic-2.0 for the released product.
resolution.selected_option: Settle the license statement in #48 or a dedicated pull request: present the Platform's Elastic-2.0 as current, keep the FSL terms labelled as the pinned Lazurio Root revision, re-pin lazurio-license to the Platform license and renew it. Recommended: it is the only way the pages stay true.
resolution.evidence: LazurioPlatform LICENSE (SHA-256 48255018…) and docs/licensing.md at fe72f68721e3; HumanAndMachines/Lazurio LICENSE.md blob 27224345 on the pin and on main; owner decision in the review thread on 2026-11-17.

issues.title: The add-device guide and Lazurio's agent manual disagree on who sets a device's `<login>-<device>` name
issues.question: Should guide/tailscale-add-device follow the agent manual of Lazurio Platform v0.1.22, in which the agent on the person's computer sets the `<login>-<device>` name on the device before approval, or should the product change to match the guide, in which nobody on the device sets it?
issues.impact: Since #68 (17 November 2026) the guide tells the person's agent not to change the device name ("do not use `--hostname`"), says that today the Organization Admin sets the name with the network operator at approval, and calls a `-1` suffix normal, to be adjusted by the Admin. The agent manual of Lazurio Platform v0.1.22, unchanged on main (`src/folder/manual.ts`, Adding a computer to a tailnet, steps 4 and 5), tells the agent on the source computer to pass `--hostname=<name>` with `--login-server` at first connection, to fix the wrong name of a device that is not yet approved with `tailscale set --hostname`, never to run `headscale nodes rename` on the Conglomerate Host, and to treat a `-1` suffix as not success. The GEN3 record `manual/operator-machine-access.md` and servers-conglomerate-host also say that the name is set on the device itself. No public source says that the Admin sets the name at approval; issue-2026-11-03-001 lists it only as a proposal. Agents with a Lazurio Folder and agents following the guide get opposite instructions. The source lazurio-device-node-names (due 2026-12-03) stays expired until this is decided.
options: Align the guide with the released product for computers: the Windows and Mac prompts set the `<login>-<device>` name on the device before approval, as the agent manual says; the sentence about the Admin setting the name today and the `-1` line follow the manual; phones keep the system's name until issue-2026-11-03-001 is resolved. Recommended: documentation does not redefine runtime behaviour, and nothing changes on servers.

Keep the guide's flow without renaming: replace the unsourced sentence with the gap (the guide does not set the name yet; Lazurio's rule sets it on the device; a clickable way is missing, issue-2026-11-03-001), and propose in LazurioPlatform that the agent manual stop requiring `--hostname` for devices added by the guide.

Change the product: the Organization Admin sets the name at approval (option 1 of issue-2026-11-03-001). This needs a LazurioPlatform decision, because the manual forbids renaming on the Conglomerate Host today; until it ships, the guide states the gap.
decision_needed_for: the Device name paragraph, the `-1` line and the agent details for Windows and macOS in guide/tailscale-add-device (en, cs)

resolution.decision: The add-device guide follows the agent manual of Lazurio Platform v0.1.22: on Windows and Mac the person's agent names the computer <login>-<device> with --hostname at its first sign-in, before approval, from the login the Organization Admin sends with the address; a phone, and a computer set up without an agent, keeps the name from the system for now (issue-2026-11-03-001); the name is never changed on the server, and a -1 suffix is not success.
resolution.rationale: Documentation does not redefine runtime behaviour; agents with a Lazurio Folder and agents following the guide now get the same instruction, and nothing changes on servers.
resolution.selected_option: Align the guide with the released product for computers: the Windows and Mac prompts set the `<login>-<device>` name on the device before approval, as the agent manual says; the sentence about the Admin setting the name today and the `-1` line follow the manual; phones keep the system's name until issue-2026-11-03-001 is resolved. Recommended: documentation does not redefine runtime behaviour, and nothing changes on servers.
resolution.evidence: LazurioPlatform src/folder/manual.ts at v0.1.22 (4e9c6b9bc25b), Adding a computer to a tailnet, steps 1 to 5, unchanged on main 7db8485; Tailscale's login takes --hostname (cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go, login.go at v1.104.5 and v1.104.7); owner decision relayed in the working thread of the review on 2026-11-17.

issues.title: Decide whether the public pages keep the GEN3 five-step order for new connections, which LazurioPlatform's Folder leaves out
issues.question: Should Lazurio's public documentation still present the order official MCP server, official CLI, Composio, reviewed open-source MCP server or CLI, supervised browser, from the GEN3 Root's external application standard, as Lazurio's current guidance for a connection that Apps → Integrations does not offer?
issues.impact: environment-app-connections, data-access-security, public-evidence, deployment-operations (step 4) and lazurio-vs-microsoft-copilot (en, cs) present the order as Lazurio's standard and link to the GEN3 Root manual, a GEN3 record since decisions 0225 and 0226. LazurioPlatform deliberately leaves it out of the Folder (`src/folder/manual.ts` at v0.1.22: "The Root's order for a new connection is left out: it puts MCP before the tool and adds paths that are no Integration's."), so agents in an Environment are never told it; LazurioPlatform issue 757 still lists it as open. data-access-security and public-evidence also link to revision 6416d27 instead of the source's pin, and public-evidence's sentence that ChatGPT apps are off is not in that revision. The Composio prompt on guide/tool-connections asks the agent to start the connection itself, which the GEN3 standard and the agent manual at v0.1.22 ("Never start a connection yourself, neither in Composio nor in Executor.") forbid in Lazurio; it is corrected together with this decision. Everything else these pages draw from the source holds against LazurioPlatform v0.1.22. The source lazurio-external-apps-current (due 2026-12-06) stays expired until this is decided.
options: Describe today's rules from LazurioPlatform (a custom MCP server goes into Executor only on the user's instruction, with the provider's official server first; no own integration without the user's decision; the forbidden list of decision 0162) and keep the five-step order only as a labelled GEN3 record, or drop it; retitle the source as a GEN3 record pinned to the root's main and align the links. Recommended: the pages then describe what the product does today, and LazurioPlatform is the authority since decision 0225.

Keep the order as Lazurio's recommendation and ask LazurioPlatform to add it to the Folder (issue 757); until then only the link pins change, and the pages keep promising a rule that agents in an Environment are not given.
Remove the order and the GEN3 link from every page and cite only environment-app-connections and LazurioPlatform's Integrations.
decision_needed_for: deployment-operations (en, cs) step 4, lazurio-vs-microsoft-copilot (en, cs) and the Composio prompt on guide/tool-connections (en, cs)

resolution.decision: The GEN3 five-step order for new connections, and the GEN3 external application standard cited as its source, are removed from every page in both locales. Where a page says how an app connects, it describes only LazurioPlatform's rule: every Integration has exactly one path (a tool from Settings → Tools, Executor, or Composio) and the user connects it; the Composio prompt on guide/tool-connections follows the same rule. The source lazurio-external-apps-current is removed, because no page needs it any more. Links to the same GEN3 document at other revisions stay where they support other statements and do not present the order: revision 3c5bda5 on reference for statements labelled as that revision (lazurio-external-apps), and revision 66e437f on provider-notes for the organization-side steps (lazurio-external-apps-org-steps); both are due on 2026-12-17.
resolution.rationale: LazurioPlatform, the authority since decisions 0225 and 0226, leaves the order out of the Folder on purpose, so the pages no longer promise a rule that agents in an Environment are not given.
resolution.selected_option: Remove the order and the GEN3 link from every page and cite only environment-app-connections and LazurioPlatform's Integrations.
resolution.evidence: LazurioPlatform docs/integrations.md (the path rule) and src/folder/manual.ts at v0.1.22, decision 0162 on main 7db8485; owner decision relayed in the working thread of the review on 2026-11-17.

issues.title: Confirm whether Organization tailnets accept the sign-in with the Lazurio account today, which decision 0246 says no tailnet uses yet
issues.question: Does a person who adds a device to an Organization's tailnet today sign in with their Lazurio account (Headscale OIDC, ending on the page "Node registered"), as guide/tailscale-add-device and the Lazurio Platform v0.1.22 agent manual say, or does no tailnet use that sign-in yet, as decision 0246 says under "What runs today"?
issues.impact: Decision 0246, identical at the source's pin 25c72bc, in release v0.1.22 and on LazurioPlatform main 7db8485, says under "What runs today": "Until Lazurio App is released, people enter as before, through the Tailscale app and the Environment's web interface ... No tailnet uses this sign-in with the Lazurio account yet". guide/tailscale-add-device (en, cs) tells people in step 3, in the Windows and Mac prompts and in the manual steps to sign in with their Lazurio account and to expect "Node registered", and guide/device-approval repeats it; the agent manual at v0.1.22 (src/folder/manual.ts, Adding a computer to a tailnet, step 4) also says the user completes OIDC sign-in with the Lazurio account. Both are Lazurio sources and they disagree on the current state, which public sources cannot settle. The source lazurio-decision-register-access-0245-0247, cited by eighteen pages, stays at its review date 2026-12-14 until this is answered; from 2026-12-15 the content check fails every pull request.
options: The sign-in with the Lazurio account runs today in the tailnets the guide is written for: the guide stays, the source is re-pinned to LazurioPlatform main with the amendments of 2026-11-17 and renewed, and an issue in LazurioPlatform asks to correct "What runs today" in decision 0246. Recommended: the guide was approved on 2026-11-17 and the released agent manual gives the same procedure, so the register's sentence is the likelier one to be out of date.

It does not run yet: guide/tailscale-add-device (step 3, the prompts, the manual steps and What happens next) and guide/device-approval describe how a device is registered today as a procedure the Organization Admin gives, the gap is recorded with a proposed product fix, and the source is renewed after the correction.

It differs between tailnets: the guide says that the sign-in with the Lazurio account works where the Organization's tailnet has it and that otherwise the Organization Admin gives the procedure; the source is renewed after the correction.

resolution.decision: People sign in to their Organization's tailnet with their Lazurio account today. guide/tailscale-add-device and guide/device-approval describe the procedure that runs and stay unchanged; the sentence in decision 0246 "What runs today" that no tailnet uses this sign-in yet is out of date and is tracked in LazurioPlatform#1086. The source lazurio-decision-register-access-0245-0247 is re-pinned to LazurioPlatform main 0eb2e3a and renewed.
resolution.rationale: The owner operates the tailnets and confirmed the current state; the agent manual of release v0.1.22 gives the same procedure, so the register's sentence is the one to correct.
resolution.selected_option: The sign-in with the Lazurio account runs today in the tailnets the guide is written for: the guide stays, the source is re-pinned to LazurioPlatform main with the amendments of 2026-11-17 and renewed, and an issue in LazurioPlatform asks to correct "What runs today" in decision 0246. Recommended: the guide was approved on 2026-11-17 and the released agent manual gives the same procedure, so the register's sentence is the likelier one to be out of date.
resolution.evidence: Owner's answer relayed in the working thread of the review on 2026-11-18 at about 23:00 UTC; LazurioPlatform src/folder/manual.ts at v0.1.22 (4e9c6b9bc25b), Adding a computer to a tailnet, step 4; decision register at 0eb2e3a, line 1319; LazurioPlatform#1086.
